target.title: fix(wizard): defer config commit until after migration apply succeeds
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

During onboarding, the migration-import flow writes the OpenClaw config file to disk before the migration provider's `apply()` runs. If `apply()` legitimately reports an error on any item, `runSetupMigrationImport()` throws, but the config is already committed with wizard metadata stamped on it. On the very next onboarding attempt, the freshness gate sees that stamped config and refuses to run the import, telling the user a fresh setup is required, even though the user is simply retrying a migration that only partially completed.

Closes #103262

## Why This Change Was Made

The config commit was placed before `provider.apply()` so that "generated reports can reference a concrete OpenClaw config target." However, the apply context already receives the in-memory config object with wizard metadata applied, which is sufficient for the provider to reference a concrete target. The disk write is only needed to persist the result, and it should only happen after apply succeeds.

The fix moves the `commitConfigFile` call from before `provider.apply()` to after `assertApplySucceeded()`. The in-memory config still has wizard metadata applied before the apply context is constructed, but the disk write only happens after apply succeeds. A failed apply no longer leaves wizard metadata on disk that blocks the next retry behind the fresh-setup gate.

## User Impact

Users who encounter a migration apply failure (due to IO errors, permission errors, malformed source files, etc.) can now simply re-run the onboarding migration-import flow without needing to manually wipe config, credentials, sessions, and workspace, or use the undocumented `OPENCLAW_MIGRATION_EXISTING_IMPORT=1` environment variable.

## Evidence

- The existing test suite mocks `runSetupMigrationImport` and does not exercise the commit ordering directly. The fix is a straightforward reordering of two lines that does not change any function signatures or return values.
- The in-memory config with wizard metadata is still available to the apply context exactly as before; only the timing of the disk write changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
